skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Create structured, test-focused implementation plans before code changes begin.
skill.summary: Turns specs into detailed implementation plans with tasks, files, tests, and handoff steps.
skill.author: obra

content.value_statement: Complex work is risky when requirements are not broken into clear steps. This skill turns specs into test-focused implementation plans for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Defines a plan header with goal, architecture, and tech stack.
Breaks work into small implementation tasks.
Lists exact files to create, modify, and test.
Includes test-first steps with expected pass and fail results.
Adds handoff guidance for executing the completed plan.
limitations: Does not inspect the repository unless the agent reads files separately.
Does not execute tests or apply code changes by itself.
Assumes the user already has a spec or requirements.
Generated file paths and commands depend on supplied context.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Build
use_cases.description: Turn a product spec into ordered tasks with files, tests, and commit checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Prepare Agent Handoff
use_cases.description: Create a plan that another Claude, Codex, or Claude Code session can execute consistently.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test-First Work
use_cases.description: Convert unclear requirements into test-first steps with expected results and review points.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Feature Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a short spec.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for this feature. Include the goal, likely files, tasks, tests, and commit points.

prompt_templates.title: Repository-Aware Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning after the agent has read relevant files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the repository context already gathered. Write a detailed plan with exact file paths, test commands, and expected outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Test-First Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning a risky refactor with behavior preservation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this refactor using TDD. Separate characterization tests, implementation tasks, regression checks, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Session Execution Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handoff across agents or sessions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan that another session can execute task by task. Include handoff notes, dependencies, verification commands, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: A request to add password reset to an existing web app.
output_examples.output: A dated plan with a goal, architecture notes, file targets, test-first tasks, verification steps, and commit checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A request to refactor billing logic without changing behavior.
output: Small refactor tasks with exact affected files.
Regression commands and expected results after each task.

output_examples.input: A request to hand work to a separate Claude Code session.
output_examples.output: A self-contained plan with context, ordered tasks, expected outputs, and clear execution handoff instructions.

best_practices: Provide the spec, constraints, and affected areas before asking for a plan.
Ask for exact file paths and test commands when repository context is available.
Review the plan before execution so outdated assumptions are corrected.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a replacement for reading the codebase.
Do not accept placeholder paths when exact files are required.
Do not execute a generated plan without checking assumptions first.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates detailed implementation plans with goals, file targets, tests, tasks, and execution handoff notes.

faq.question: Does it write code changes?
faq.answer: No. It prepares a plan before code changes begin.

faq.question: Can it be used with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The plan format is useful for Codex, Claude, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after you have requirements and before implementation starts.

faq.question: Does it require repository context?
faq.answer: Repository context is not required, but it improves file paths, test commands, and task order.

faq.question: How should I review the output?
faq.answer: Check assumptions, file paths, test coverage, and task order before execution.
